title: Metric prefixes, from tera to pico
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Every metric unit uses the same set of prefixes, so learning these twelve unlocks meters, grams, liters, watts and bytes all at once. Each step is a power of ten, which is what makes the metric system easy to convert.

How to hold it: Build from first principles: each prefix means 'times ten to some power.' From kilo down to milli the steps go one power of ten at a time (kilo, hecto, deka, base, deci, centi, milli: "Kind Hippos Dance Barefoot During Chilly Mornings"), and outside that range they jump three powers at a time (mega, giga, tera; micro, nano, pico). Chunk them that way: the big jumps, the small steps, the tiny jumps.
